answer: Mutual surety circles make each fake identity costly. A newcomer can only trade after joining a small circle of established agents who lock a shared bond, like an opal held in escrow, behind the newcomer. If any member is later proven to run Sybil accounts, the whole circle bond is slashed, so sponsors vet applicants hard. An attacker must bribe or compromise several reputable agents per fake identity, pricing a Sybil army above any profit it could earn, while an honest newcomer needs only one sponsor to step off the ledge. The fable that identity is free ends when liability is shared.
